display.title: Episode 555: A Time to Remember, and Ani Maamin (Asarah B'Teves)
display.summary_short: On Asarah B'Teves, Uncle Yossi explains why we remember the siege of Yerushalayim, two brothers who say the Twelve Pesukim lead the Shema, and a young guest sings Ani Maamin.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Asarah B'Teves 5753. Uncle Yossi explains, with Shlomo HaMelech's words 'there is a time for everything', that there is a time to be happy and a time to be sad, not to stay sad but to learn from the past and improve. On the tenth of Teves, Nevuchadnetzar's armies began their siege of Yerushalayim; after two and a half years the walls were breached on the seventeenth of Tammuz, and three weeks later, on Tisha B'Av, the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed. As long as we learn Torah and keep mitzvos, Hashem, the Guardian of Israel, protects us, and He has promised that these fast days will become days of joy when Moshiach comes. Two brothers, who say the Twelve Pesukim and encourage their friends to do so, lead the Shema; then come tzedakah, Tehillim for the Rebbe's recovery and an advertisement. A young guest sings 'Ani Maamin', the song of our belief in Moshiach's coming, and tells how much he enjoys being a member of Tzivos Hashem and reading the Moshiach Times.
display.lesson: We remember sad days in order to learn from the past and improve, and we believe that Moshiach will turn them into days of joy.

date.note: 'Today is the tenth day of the month Teves'; 10 Teves 5753 was Sunday 3 Jan 1993, a week after ep. 554 (Zos Chanukah).
